messages.subject: workflowrBeta: A permanent home for the beta release of workflowr
messages.subject_clean: workflowrBeta: A permanent home for the beta release of workflowr
messages.body_plain:
Hi workflowr users!

I am working on some cool new features for workflowr, e.g. the ability to easily view past versions of your webpages. However, this also involves some backwards-incompatible changes. The extra infrastructure files, e.g. chunks.R, will be removed in future releases. This will make it easier for users to update in the future (since you won't have to edit files in your repo).

But do not fret if you like your current setup! Migrating to the new setup will be straightforward (I'll include detailed instructions), but if you'd prefer to keep everything the same, I have created a new repository, workflowrBeta, that will continue to support the beta release with future bug fixes and other minor patches.

https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowrBeta

Thanks for using workflowr!

John

messages.subject: Release candidate for workflowr 1.0 ready for testing
messages.subject_clean: Release candidate for workflowr 1.0 ready for testing
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm excited to announce that a release candidate <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/tree/dev#readme> for workflowr 1.0 is ready for testing!

The 1.0 release is a big change. Instead of relying on the external code chunks in `chunks.R` to implement the reproducibility features, workflowr 1.0 replaces `chunks.R` with the output format `wflow_html()` and site generator`wflow_site()`. This enables a much more informative reproducibility report to be created.

One of the coolest new features is that it includes links to GitHub to past versions of the HTML and figure files.

I've attached the full release notes if you're interested in learning about all the new changes.

Installation

Install the release candidate 0.11.0.9000 from the dev branch:

devtools::install_github("jdblischak/workflowr@dev")

When you're finished testing, you can re-install the current stable version:

devtools::install_github("jdblischak/workflowr")

Testing the new features

To see the new features, you can start a new project like you did in the past:

library("workflowr")
wflow_start("testproject")
wflow_build()

Note that the online documentation is still for the stable version. To learn about the new features to be introduced in 1.0, read the help file ?wflow_html.

Updating an existing project

There is no need to update an existing project. The 1.0 version of workflowr is backwards-compatible as long as you do not run `wflow_update()`. And if you do notice a difference in behavior, you can always re-install workflowr from workflowrBeta <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowrBeta>.

However, the advantages of workflowr 1.0 are best seen on existing project with many past versions.

# Preview the files that will be updated
wflow_update()
# Update the files
wflow_update(dry_run = FALSE)
# Preview the updates
wflow_build()

And since you are using Git, you can always discard these changes with `git checkout` or `git reset` (please feel free to contact me for assistance with this).

See ?wflow_update for more details.

Feedback

I would love any feedback you have. Please contact me with your thoughts however is most convenient for you (email, Twitter DM, Slack). If you find a bug or have a concrete proposal, please open an Issue on GitHub <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues>.

Thanks!

John

messages.subject: workflowr 1.0.1 has been released!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

The new version of workflowr <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/releases> is now the default. Please give it a try! To see the new features in action, see this video demonstration <https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O1wv94sZfvE>.

I am now working on submitting the package to CRAN.

John

messages.subject: workflowr now officially on CRAN!
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This morning workflowr was published on CRAN <https://cran.r-project.org/package=workflowr>. You can now easily install workflowr with install.packages:

install.packages("workflowr")

And please remember to send any feature requests or feedback to the GitHub Issues <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues>. The new "reproducibility report" is still in development, so you can help shape its features and appearance.

John
